issues.title: [Feature]: TRTLLM-GEN FMHA graph-safe request permutation and length-aware scheduling for ragged decode
issues.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet.

### Problem

TRTLLM-GEN paged decode loses substantial throughput when requests in the same batch have highly variable KV lengths. An experimental SGLang-side prototype demonstrates that two forms of length-aware scheduling can recover this loss:

- For batch sizes at or below the SM count, partitioning length-sorted requests into a small number of subgroups improves CTA allocation and reduces the longest-KV tail within each launch.
- For batch sizes above the SM count, keeping one persistent FMHA launch but changing request-entry order reduces persistent-scheduler tail imbalance.

On 4 x GB300 with Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4-V2, the prototype improves full-model fixed-acceptance output throughput by a geometric mean of **6.816% across eight formally valid AgentX-ragged points**, while all ten uniform-length controls remain within the -1% no-regression gate. At B192, the full-model gain is **10.846%** and the same persistent FMHA kernel is **34.39% faster for Q1** after request reordering.

The measured prototype demonstrates that the performance is recoverable, but it requires serving-layer tensor permutation, output scatter, multiple CUDA Graph variants, and serial subgroup launches. We would like to discuss two FlashInfer capabilities:

1. An optional graph-safe request-order indirection for TRTLLM-GEN FMHA.
2. Longer term, a kernel-owned length-aware work scheduler for the low-batch ragged regime.

The table below reports full-model fixed-acceptance output tok/s/GPU. `Control mean` is the mean of same-node control runs immediately before and after the prototype run. issues.title: [Bug] SM121 (DGX Spark GB10): mixed mxfp8 x mxfp4 fused MoE dies in moe_sort routing with "no kernel image is available" from a prebuilt moe_utils .so that has no SM12x image
issues.body:
## 🐛 Bug

On NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM121 / compute_121a, major version **12**), the mixed-precision CuTe-DSL path `cute_dsl_fused_moe_mxfp8_mxfp4` fails inside its routing step with `no kernel image is available for execution on the device`, raised from a **prebuilt** `moe_utils` shared object that only contains SM100-family images.

Related: PR #5237 fixes the *first* SM121 blocker in this module (the JIT arch filter `supported_major_versions=[9, 10]` -> adds `12`). With that fix applied, the JIT path builds `sm121a` cubins fine on this machine — but the mixed path still dies at routing time because a prebuilt, SM100-only `moe_utils` artifact takes precedence over the local JIT build.

## To Reproduce

Environment: DGX Spark GB10 (SM121), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer 0.6.18 (SGLang image), flashinfer-jit-cache + cubin wheels installed.

1. Apply the PR #5237 one-liner (bind-mount `flashinfer/jit/moe_utils.py` with `supported_major_versions=[10, 12]` on 0.6.18) so that JIT compilation of `moe_utils` succeeds at all.
2. Call the mixed MoE:

```python
import torch
from flashinfer.fused_moe.cute_dsl import cute_dsl_fused_moe_mxfp8_mxfp4
# minimal call per docstring; real geometry used on our side:
#   num_experts=192, top_k=6, hidden=5120, intermediate=1152, EP2
out = cute_dsl_fused_moe_mxfp8_mxfp4(x, x_sf, topk_ids, topk_scales,
                                     w1, w1_sf, w1_alpha, w2, w2_sf, w2_alpha,
                                     num_experts=192, top_k=6)
```

3. It dies inside `moe_sort` (routing), before any GEMM:

```
RuntimeError: Error in function 'operator()' at /workspace/csrc/fused_moe/trtllm_backend/trtllm_fused_moe_routing_custom.cu:306: ... no kernel image is available for execution on the device
```

The `/workspace/csrc/...` path is the CI build container's source path (ci/bash.sh mounts the workspace at `/workspace`), i.e. the error comes from a `.so` that was compiled ahead-of-time upstream, not from the local JIT build.

Note `cute_dsl_fused_moe_mxfp8_mxfp4` and its wrapper class carry `@supported_compute_capability([100, 103])`, but that decorator only attaches metadata (`_supported_ccs` + `is_compute_capability_supported`); it does not gate the call, so on SM121 the function body runs and reaches the routing kernel.

## Root-cause analysis (from source)

The call chain is `cute_dsl_fused_moe_mxfp8_mxfp4` -> `moe_sort` -> `_get_moe_utils_module()` -> `gen_moe_utils_module().build_and_load()` (flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/moe_utils.py). The `moe_utils` JitSpec compiles `trtllm_fused_moe_routing_custom.cu` among its sources — so the routing kernels that fail are inside the `moe_utils` module.

Two upstream factors combine on SM121:

1. **AOT registration is SM100-family-only.** In `flashinfer/aot.py` (both v0.6.18 and current main), `gen_moe_utils_module()` is only appended under `if has_sm100f:`. `detect_sm_capabilities()` derives `has_sm100f` from `compute_100` appearing in `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST`. An SM121 provider build (`FLASHINFER_JIT_CACHE_PROVIDER_ARCH=12.1a` or similar) has no `compute_100` in its arch list, so the packaged `moe_utils` artifact is only ever built for SM100-family provider wheels — and even those are compiled with `[10]`-filtered flags (pre-#5237), never `sm121a`.

2. **`try_load()` prefers the AOT artifact unconditionally when the shim is installed.** `JitSpecNvcc.try_load()` (flashinfer/jit/core.py) returns the AOT `.so` from `FLASHINFER_AOT_DIR` (`flashinfer-jit-c

issues.title: [Bug] CUTLASS NVFP4 MoE rejects Relu2 intermediate_size=1856 due to scale-factor alignment mismatch
issues.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find an existing report for this NVFP4 alignment mismatch.

## Environment

- FlashInfer version: `0.6.18`
- FlashInfer commit: `4927c0e`
- GPU: NVIDIA B300 (`NVIDIA_B300_SXM6_AC`)
- CUDA: 13.0
- Python: 3.12
- Container: `flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-cu130:20260811-e673f7f`
- Routine/backend: `cutlass_fused_moe` / CUTLASS NVFP4

## Bug description

`cutlass_fused_moe` rejects the valid non-gated Nemotron-3-Nano shape `hidden_size=2688, intermediate_size=1856` when using NVFP4 weights and `Relu2` activation.

The benchmark prepares the FC1 scale-factor N dimension with 128-element padding, so 1856 is padded to 1920. The CUTLASS binding validates that N dimension using `MinKDimAlignmentNVFP4` (64) instead of `MinNDimAlignmentNVFP4` (128), and therefore expects 1856. The resulting 1920-vs-1856 mismatch triggers the shape assertion.

Expected behavior: the non-gated NVFP4 case should run successfully with the real model dimensions. Dimensions should not need to be changed to 1920 merely to bypass validation.

## Minimal reproduction

```bash
python3 benchmarks/flashinfer_benchmark.py \
  --routine cutlass_fused_moe \
  --num_tokens 1 \
  --hidden_size 2688 \
  --intermediate_size 1856 \
  --num_experts 128 \
  --top_k 6 \
  --cutlass_variant nvfp4 \
  --input_dtype bfloat16 \
  --activation-type Relu2 \
  --verbose \
  --generate_repro_command \
  --case_tag Nemotron-3-Nano-decode
```

## Error messages / logs

```text
[ERROR] Error running test: --routine cutlass_fused_moe --num_tokens 1 --hidden_size 2688 --intermediate_size 1856 --num_experts 128 --top_k 6 --cutlass_variant nvfp4 --input_dtype bfloat16 --activation-type Relu2 --verbose --generate_repro_command --case_tag "Nemotron-3-Nano-decode"
[ERROR] Error: Check failed: (fc1_weight_block.size(0) == num_experts_on_rank && fc1_weight_block.size(1) == TmaWarpSpecializedGroupedGemmInput::alignToSfDim(inter_size, TmaWarpSpecializedGroupedGemmInput::MinKDimAlignmentNVFP4) && fc1_weight_block.size(2) * FP8_PER_INT32 * TmaWarpSpecializedGroupedGemmInput::NVFP4BlockScaleVectorSize == TmaWarpSpecializedGroupedGemmInput::alignToSfDim(hidden_size, TmaWarpSpecializedGroupedGemmInput::MinKDimAlignmentNVFP4)) is false: fc1 weight block size must be (num_experts_on_rank, inter_size, hidden_size // 4 // block_scale_vector_size)
```

## Additional context

The likely faulty check is in `csrc/fused_moe/cutlass_backend/flashinfer_cutlass_fused_moe_binding.cu`, in the NVFP4 branch of `getQuantParams()`. FC1's outer/N dimension is checked with `MinKDimAlignmentNVFP4`; it appears that `MinNDimAlignmentNVFP4` should be used instead.

This is related to, but distinct from, #2731: that issue covered hardcoded gated-activation multipliers in MXFP8 paths, while this report concerns NVFP4 N/K scale-factor alignment.

issues.title: [CI] Invalid top-k grouping in GLM-5 and Kimi-K2.5 NVFP4 MoE benchmarks
issues.body:
## Problem

python3 flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe --num_tokens 64 --hidden_size 6144 --intermediate_size 2048 --num_experts 256 --top_k 8 --n_group 1 --topk_group 1 --routed_scaling_factor 2.5 --use_routing_bias --routing_method deepseek_v3 --use_shuffled_weight --activation-type Swiglu --fp4_mode nvfp4 --verbose --generate_repro_command --case_tag GLM-5-NVFP4

## Actual behavior

issues.title: trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe fails to reshape GPT-OSS-120B MXFP4 inputs on B300 and GB300

issues.title: [Performance] SM120 NVFP4 paged causal prefill is ~1.7-1.8x slower than FP8
issues.body:
## Summary

On SM120, FlashInfer's paged causal prefill with BF16 queries and an NVFP4 KV cache is about **1.7-1.8x slower than the matched FP8 KV-cache path** in our vLLM workload.

NVFP4 decode is faster than FP8 as expected for a bandwidth-bound workload, so the regression appears localized to the compute-heavy causal prefill path.

## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell (SM120)
- CUDA: 12.9
- PyTorch: 2.10.0+cu129
- FlashInfer: 0.6.15
- KV layout: HND
- Query dtype: BF16 at the model boundary (quantized as required by the selected path)
- KV formats compared:
  - NVFP4 packed data with per-16-element FP8 scale factors
  - FP8 KV cache
- Integration: vLLM FlashInfer backend

## Matched profile results

The two traces contain some disjoint startup/warmup regions, so the table below compares the same 48 causal paged-prefill calls.

| KV cache | Calls | Total | Mean per call |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| NVFP4 | 48 | 145.81 ms | 3.04 ms |
| FP8 | 48 | 84.03 ms | 1.75 ms |

**NVFP4 / FP8 prefill ratio: 1.74x**

For context, in the same workload:

| Operation | NVFP4 | FP8 | Observation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Decode | 9.63 us | 12.35 us | NVFP4 is about 22% faster |
| KV append | 8.39 us | 3.01 us | NVFP4 is slower, but only about 7 ms total |
| Matched CUTLASS segment | 93.61 ms | 96.69 ms | Similar |
| All matched kernels | 297.73 ms | 238.45 ms | Prefill explains most of the gap |

The end-to-end capacity test also shows the tradeoff: NVFP4 avoids preemption and admits more concurrent requests, but wall time is worse because prefill is slower.

## Current hypothesis

The current SM120 FA2 NVFP4 prefill path appears to consume packed FP4 KV through an unpack/convert/scale sequence before the BF16-oriented QK MMA. In causal prefill, QK is compute-heavy and the reduced KV memory traffic does not offset that extra conversion work.

This is a hypothesis based on the kernel path and profile behavior, not yet a complete instruction-level Nsight Compute proof.

An A4Q-style path could avoid this cost by quantizing Q and using native block-scaled FP4 QK MMA (`use_nvf4_qk`-style dispatch), while retaining the packed NVFP4 KV representation.

## Questions

1. Is this performance behavior expected for the current SM120 NVFP4 paged-prefill implementation?
2. Is an A4Q/native block-scaled FP4 QK path planned for upstream FlashInfer?
3. Would maintainers accept a contribution wiring Q quantization and block-scaled FP4 MMA into the paged causal prefill path?
4. Are there existing benchmarks or recommended kernel parameters for comparing NVFP4 and FP8 prefill fairly on SM120?

## Related work

- vLLM tracking issue with the serving-level measurements: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50416
- NVFP4 KV support for prefill/batch attention: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3097
- SM120/121 NVFP4 paged-prefill extensions: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3684

I can provide the Nsight Systems JSON traces and a reduced benchmark case if that would help with kernel-level investigation.

issues.title: DGX Spark (SM121) Current Support Audit
issues.body:
# FlashInfer — DGX Spark (SM121) Current Support Audit

**Date:** 2026-04-24
**Scope:** Audit of SM121 (compute capability 12.1, DGX Spark) support across FlashInfer ops, APIs, backends, and testing.
**Goal:** Improve Spark usability on FlashInfer by identifying existing gaps.

**Note: skip to "15. Consolidated Action Items" for TLDR.**

---

## Architecture Context

| Gencode | Target | CUDA Requirement |
|---------|--------|------------------|
| `compute_120a` / `sm_120a` | RTX 5090 (SM120) | CUDA 12.8 |
| `compute_120f` / `sm_120f` | SM12x family (120 + 121) | CUDA 12.9 |
| `compute_121a` / `sm_121a` | DGX Spark (SM121) | CUDA 12.9 |

### SM120 vs SM121: Implications for FlashInfer

Per the [CUDA 13.2 Programming Guide — Compute Capabilities](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.2.0/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html) (Tables 29–33), SM120 and SM121 share a single "12.x" spec column: identical shared memory (99 KB/block, 100 KB/SM), warps (48/SM), registers (64K/SM), tensor core data types (TF32, BF16, FP16, FP8, FP6, FP4, INT8), TMA, and cluster support. [Table 28](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.2.0/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html#compute-capabilities-family-specific-compatibility) confirms `compute_120f` is compatible with **both** CC 12.0 and 12.1. The chip-level differences (SM121 = aarch64 host, unified LPDDR5x, 84 SMs vs SM120's x86_64, discrete GDDR7, up to 170 SMs) do not affect kernel correctness — only SM-count-based heuristics and host toolchain.

### `f` vs `a` compilation targets: performance implications

Per the [PTX ISA 9.3](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/index.html) (§9.7.15.5.14 for dense `mma`, §9.7.15.6.3 for sparse `mma.sp`), `120f` (family) is a subset of `120a`/`121a` (arch-specific). Most SM12x features — including **dense** NVFP4/MXFP4 block-scaled MMA — are family-specific and available via `120f` from PTX ISA 8.8. The arch-specific restriction (requiring `sm_120a`/`sm_121a`) applies **only to sparse MMA** (`mma.sp`) with `.kind::mxf4nvf4`/`.kind::mxf4`:

| PTX Feature | `compute_120` (baseline) | `compute_120f` (family) | `compute_120a` / `compute_121a` (arch) |
|-------------|--------------------------|------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| FP4/FP6/FP8 conversions (`cvt`) | No | Yes | Yes |
| FP4/FP6 MMA, block-scaled MMA (`.kind::mxf8f6f4`) | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Dense** NVFP4 MMA (`.kind::mxf4nvf4`) | No | **Yes** (PTX ISA ≥ 8.8) | **Yes** |
| **Dense** MXFP4 MMA (`.kind::mxf4`) | No | **Yes** (PTX ISA ≥ 8.8) | **Yes** |
| **Sparse** NVFP4 MMA (`mma.sp` `.kind::mxf4nvf4`) | No | **No** | **Yes** |
| **Sparse** MXFP4 MMA (`mma.sp` `.kind::mxf4`) | No | **No** | **Yes** |

FlashInfer's b12x GEMM kernel (`dense_blockscaled_gemm_sm120_b12x.py`) uses `cute.nvgpu.warp.MmaMXF4NVF4Op` — a **dense** block-scaled MMA atom. This means `sm_120f` wheels already emit native NVFP4/MXFP4 dense MMA instructions. Only **sparse** NVFP4/MXFP4 MMA (not currently used in FlashInfer) requires `sm_120a`/`sm_121a`.

> **Correction (2026-06-12):** An earlier version of this table stated that ALL `.kind::mxf4nvf4`/`.kind::mxf4` MMA was arch-specific-only. Per [Harry-Chen's feedback](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3170#issuecomment-4677810517) and PTX ISA §9.7.15.5.14 vs §9.7.15.6.3, the restriction is limited to the sparse (`mma.sp`) variant.

### Wheel build arch targets

The release whe

issues.title: [Bug] sm12x MoE CuTe-DSL kernels are never disk-cached — cute.compile hardcodes no_cache=True, so every fresh engine re-pays 15–40 s MLIR compiles per kernel shape
issues.body:
## Summary

The Blackwell sm12x fused-MoE path compiles all of its CuTe-DSL kernels through explicit
`cute.compile(...)`, which unconditionally disables the DSL's file cache. The only caching
layer is three in-process Python dicts, so **every engine start re-pays the full MLIR JIT
cost for every kernel specialization it touches** — measured at **~40 s** for the dynamic
kernel's first hit and **~15–18 s per small-`m` micro-kernel specialization**. In a serving
context (vLLM `--moe-backend=flashinfer_b12x`) these compiles land mid-request and freeze
the whole engine (vllm#47458: ~17.5 s stop-the-world stalls, all in-flight requests frozen
including mid-decode).

`CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR` / `CUTE_DSL_DISABLE_FILE_CACHING` have no effect on this path — the
gate that would consult them is short-circuited before they are read.

## Environment

- flashinfer 0.6.12, 0.6.13, and **0.6.15.post1** (all verified; `moe_dispatch.py` cache
  structure unchanged across them)
- nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.0 and **4.6.0** (both verified)
- SM120: RTX 5070 Ti (×2, TP/PP), RTX 5090 (unsharded), RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell — reproduced
  on all three in the vllm#47458 thread
- Model: `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` via vLLM `--moe-backend=flashinfer_b12x`

## Mechanism (exact code paths)

1. **The DSL hardcodes `no_cache=True` for explicit compiles.**
   `CompileCallable._compile` sets `kwargs["no_cache"] = True` unconditionally:
   - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.0: `base_dsl/compiler.py:604-605`
   - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.0: `base_dsl/compiler.py:1319`

2. **The file cache is gated behind `if not no_cache`** — both the load and the dump —
   so the env vars are never even consulted for explicit compiles:
   - 4.5.0: `base_dsl/dsl.py:1645` (load), `:1736` (dump)
   - 4.6.0: `base_dsl/dsl.py:2004` (load), `:2105` (dump); in-memory `jit_cache` lookups
     likewise skipped under `no_cache` at `:2012`, `:2293`

3. **The sm12x MoE dispatch only ever compiles through `cute.compile`,** with plain
   in-process dicts on top — nothing reaches disk:
   - 0.6.12/0.6.13: `blackwell_sm12x/moe_dispatch.py:676/912/1675` (compile sites);
     `_STATIC/_MICRO/_DYNAMIC_KERNEL_CACHE`
   - 0.6.15.post1: compile sites at `:697/:942/:1723`; caches at `:486/:733/:1524`

4. Compounding factor (tracked separately as #3836): the micro-kernel `cache_key`
   includes both `m` and `workspace.max_rows` (0.6.15.post1 `moe_dispatch.py:770-791`,
   fields at `:774`/`:778`), so workspace growth invalidates already-compiled small-batch
   entries even *within* a process lifetime. With no disk layer underneath, each
   invalidation is a full 15 s+ recompile, not a reload.

## Verification

Behavioral check from the vllm#47458 thread (credit @waynehacking8, on 0.6.12 / DSL 4.5.0):

- `cute.compile` of a trivial `@cute.jit` function leaves `CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR` **empty**.
- Calling the same jit function **directly** (implicit compile path) writes
  `cute_dsl_<hash>.mlir`, and a fresh process then logs `JIT cache hit IN-FILE`.
- Only the implicit direct-call path caches; flashinfer's MoE dispatch never uses it.

Source-level re-verification on 0.6.15.post1 / DSL 4.6.0 (2026-08-02, inside the
`vllm/vllm-openai` nightly image): every line cite in the Mechanism section above was
confirmed against the installed packages — the hardcoded `no_cache=True`, the
`if not no_cache` gates around both file-cache load and dump, the three `cute.compile`
sites, the three in-process dicts, and `m`/`max_rows` still present in the micr

为 FA2 的 flash_attn_with_kvcache 添加 Varlen 支持
maintainer_path: 通过修复 Python DSL 的路由与 JIT 边界问题，熟悉 FA4 的编译期拦截机制。
通过离线编译与 PTX 静态分析，解决 SM100 复杂的异步流水线死锁问题，建立在核心 Kernel 层的技术威信。
维护 FA2 的 C++ 遗留代码，确保向后兼容性，逐步接管编译期静态分析工具链的所有权。

positioning.overview:
FlashAttention 是目前深度学习领域最核心的底层算子库之一，其核心价值在于通过硬件感知（IO-Awareness）的精确注意力机制，打破了 Transformer 模型的显存墙与算力瓶颈。对于你这样一位资深 GPU kernel 工程师来说，这个仓库目前正处于一个极具技术挑战和范式转移的阶段：项目正在从传统的 C++/CUDA/CuTe 实现（FA2 位于 `csrc/`，FA3 位于 `hopper/`）全面向基于 Python 的领域特定语言（DSL）迁移。最新的 FlashAttention-4（FA4）完全使用 Python 编写，基于 `CuTeDSL`（NVIDIA CUTLASS DSL），并在运行时通过 `apache-tvm-ffi` JIT 编译为 PTX/CUBIN，专门针对 SM90 (Hopper) 和 SM100/SM110 (Blackwell) 架构进行极致优化。

针对你的**硬约束（只有 Mac，无本地 GPU，仅有 Colab T4）**，这个仓库的 FA4 架构为你提供了一个极其罕见的切入机会：根据 `CLAUDE.md` 的证据，FA4 支持 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1` 环境变量。这意味着你可以**完全在 Apple Silicon 的 CPU 上，利用 PyTorch FakeTensor 模式并行编译所有 Kernel 生成 PTX/CUBIN，而无需分配任何 GPU 显存**。你可以结合仓库中 `AI/` 目录下的静态分析工具（如 `SASS_MMA_ANALYSIS.md`, `parse_clc_log.py`），在 Mac 上纯靠阅读和分析生成的 SASS/PTX 指令来做性能调优和指令级 debug。

**重要警告**：你计划用 Colab 免费的 T4 (SM75) 做最终验证是**行不通的**。FA4 的指令集（TMA, GMMA）强依赖 SM90+，T4 根本无法运行这些 Kernel。你的整个开发闭环必须依赖于 Mac 上的离线编译与静态 SASS 分析，这极其考验你对底层指令的盲写与推演能力，但这也正是你作为资深专家的核心壁垒所在。
positioning.problem: 解决标准 Attention 机制中 O(N^2) 复杂度导致的 HBM 显存带宽瓶颈（Memory Wall）问题。通过 SRAM Tiling、重计算（Recomputation）以及利用新一代 GPU 的 TMA（张量内存加速器）和 GMMA（异步矩阵乘），实现极高算力利用率（MFU）的精确注意力计算，同时解决变长序列（Varlen）、GQA/MQA、Paged KV Cache 以及稀疏注意力（如 Sparse MLA）在极端硬件下的调度与寄存器溢出问题。
positioning.users: 大模型（LLM）、视觉语言模型（VLM）及扩散模型（如 DiT/视频生成）的底层架构师、训练加速工程师、推理引擎（如 vLLM, TensorRT-LLM）开发者，以及 PyTorch/HuggingFace 等框架的算子集成维护者。

landscape.difference: SDPA 是高层 API，底层通常会路由调用 FlashAttention。但 FA 仓库永远领先于 PyTorch Core，例如 FA4 的 SM100 支持、CuTeDSL 架构和 Sparse MLA 目前只能在 FA 仓库中体验到。
Meta 维护的库，早期有自己的 memory-efficient attention 实现，但现在其核心注意力机制已重度依赖并封装 FlashAttention。FA 更偏向极致的单点 Kernel 突破，xFormers 更偏向模型组件的工程化封装。
Triton 提供了更易读的 Python 编译器方案，但在极限性能（特别是针对特定架构如 SM100 的 TMA/GMMA 细粒度控制、寄存器分配、Epilogue 融合）上，FA 基于 CuTe/CuTeDSL 的手写/JIT 方案上限更高。注：FA 仓库的 AMD ROCm 分支 (`third_party/aiter`) 实际上使用了 Triton 后端。
vLLM 侧重于系统级的 KV Cache 显存管理（分页），而 FA 侧重于单算子的计算密度。FA 内部也实现了 Paged KV 的 Kernel（如 `hopper/paged_kv.h`），常被推理框架作为底层依赖提取。

positioning.stage: 处于 FA3 到 FA4 的剧烈架构演进期。FA4 处于高频迭代的 Beta 阶段（2026年9月已发布至 v4.0.0.beta31），核心开发精力全部集中在基于 CuTeDSL 的 SM90/SM100 优化上。

codemap.layers:
针对你目前只有 MacBook Air (Apple Silicon) 的硬约束，FlashAttention-4 (FA4) 的架构分层对你来说是一个完美的「离线编译与静态分析」游乐场。FA4 彻底抛弃了传统的 C++/CUDA 混合编程范式，转向了基于 Python 的 CuTeDSL。整个系统可以分为以下五个核心层次：

1. **API 与路由层 (API & Routing Layer)**：位于 `flash_attn/cute/interface.py`。这是 PyTorch 与底层 Kernel 的交汇点。它负责接收 Tensor，提取 shape/stride/dtype，并处理 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1` 环境变量。在你的 Mac 上，这一层会拦截真实的显存分配，仅传递元数据（Metadata）给下游。

2. **DSL 核心表达层 (DSL Kernel Layer)**：位于 `flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd*.py` 和 `flash_bwd*.py`。这是你未来工作的主阵地。Kernel 完全使用 Python 编写，通过 `@cute.jit` 装饰器标记。在这里，你使用 Python 语法定义 TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator) 描述符、Shared Memory 布局（Swizzle）、以及 MMA (Matrix Multiply-Accumulate) 原子操作。

3. **调度与流水线层 (Scheduling & Pipeline Layer)**：位于 `flash_attn/cute/tile_scheduler.py` 和 `pipeline.py`。为了榨干 SM90/SM100 的算力，FA4 将调度逻辑从 Kernel 中解耦。包含静态调度 (Static)、动态持久化调度 (Dynamic Persistent) 以及集群启动控制 (CLC, Cluster Launch Control)。流水线层则通过 `PipelineStateSimple` 管理 TMA/GMMA/UMMA 的异步多缓冲（Multi-buffering）状态和 Phase Bit 翻转。

4. **硬件原语抽象层 (Hardware Intrinsics Layer)**：位于 `flash_attn/cute/blackwell_helpers.py`、`ampere_helpers.py` 和 `barrier.py`。这里封装了极底层的 PTX 指令，例如 SM100 的 `tcgen05.mma` (Tensor Core Gen 5)、`ld.global.acquire` (异步屏障获取) 等。通过 MLIR 的 `llvm.inline_asm` 注入。

5. **JIT 编译与静态分析层 (JIT & Static Analysis Layer)**：这是你在 Mac 上闭环的最关键层。底层依赖 `apache-tvm-ffi` 将 Python AST 降级为 MLIR，再编译为 PTX/CUBIN。配合 `AI/` 目录下的工具（如 `parse_clc_log.py` 和 `SASS_MMA_ANALYSIS.md`），你可以在 CPU 上完成编译，并纯靠阅读生成的 SASS/PTX 指令来推演寄存器溢出（Register Spilling）和 TMA 访存冲突（Hazard）。

modules.role: 对外暴露 PyTorch 接口，处理 FakeTensor 模式的路由，提取 Tensor 元数据并分发给对应的 JIT Kernel。
modules.notes: 在 Mac 上调试时，这里是 FakeTensor 注入的起点，确保不会触发真实的 CUDA 显存分配。

modules.role: FA4 的前向核心实现，包含 SM90 (Hopper) 和 SM100 (Blackwell) 的具体逻辑，定义 TMA Load 和 MMA 计算循环。
modules.notes: 重点关注 `flash_fwd_sm100.py` 和 `flash_fwd_sm90.py`，这是你做指令级优化的核心文件。

modules.role: FA4 的反向传播实现，极其复杂。包含 dK/dV 和 dQ 的分离计算，以及针对 SM100 HD256 的特殊 2-CTA 协同优化。
modules.notes: 最近提交热点（Sparse MLA bwd, HD256 2-CTA），反向逻辑的寄存器压力极大，是 SASS 调优的重灾区。

modules.role: 管理 Block 级别的任务分发，支持 Static, Dynamic 和 CLC (Cluster Launch Control) 调度模式。
modules.notes: 决定了 MFU (算力利用率) 的上限，特别是 Varlen (变长序列) 场景下的负载均衡。

modules.role: 管理异步流水线状态，处理 Circular Buffer 的 Index 和 Phase Bit，确保 TMA 和 MMA 的异步并发。
modules.notes: 通过位运算 (`divmod` 优化) 管理 Phase，是理解 Hopper/Blackwell 异步编程模型的关键。

modules.role: 封装 SM100 (Blackwell) 特有的硬件原语，如 `tcgen05` (第五代 Tensor Core) 的 MMA 指令和 PTX 内联汇编。
modules.notes: 如果你要盲写 SM100 优化，必须熟读此文件中的 `tcgen05.Field.ACCUMULATE` 等底层控制逻辑。

modules.role: 提供 CTA 间和 Cluster 间的底层同步原语，直接映射到 PTX 的 `ld.acquire` 和 `red.release`。
modules.notes: 多 CTA 协作（如 SM100 2-CTA bwd）的基石，死锁排查的重点关注对象。

modules.role: 提供离线 SASS/PTX 分析工具、TMA 冲突检查和 CLC 日志解析。这是你在 Mac 上进行性能调优的「眼睛」。
modules.notes: 你的核心武器库。在没有物理 GPU 的情况下，依靠这些工具分析编译产物来验证你的 Kernel 优化。

modules.role: FA4 的测试用例集，支持通过环境变量开启 FakeTensor 模式进行全量并行编译。
modules.notes: 使用 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1 pytest -n 64` 在 Mac 上触发编译闭环。

modules.role: 上一代基于 C++/CuTe 的 SM90 实现，目前作为 FA4 的对照组和稳定版存在。
modules.notes: 当你在 FA4 的 Python DSL 中遇到行为不符合预期时，可以来这里翻阅 C++ 源码作为 Ground Truth。

codemap.data_flow:
针对你只有 Mac 的硬约束，以下是一次**完全在 CPU 上执行的 FakeTensor 编译与静态分析数据流**，这是你日常开发的核心闭环：

1. **入口触发 (Test Invocation)**：你在 Mac 终端运行 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1 FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1 pytest -n 64 tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py`。环境变量 `FAKE_TENSOR=1` 是整个流程的灵魂，它告诉 PyTorch 不要分配任何真实的 GPU 显存（Mac 也没有 Nvidia GPU），而是创建仅包含 shape、stride 和 dtype 信息的虚拟张量（FakeTensors）。

2. **API 路由与元数据提取 (API Routing)**：测试用例调用 `flash_attn/cute/interface.py` 中的 `flash_attn_func`。接口层接收到 FakeTensors Q, K, V 后，提取其维度信息（如 batch_size, seqlen, headdim=256）。根据这些元数据和硬件架构（假设目标是 SM100），接口层计算出 Grid Shape，并选择合适的调度器（如 `ClcSchedulerState`）。

3. **DSL Kernel 实例化 (DSL Instantiation)**：控制流进入 `@cute.jit` 装饰的 Python Kernel（例如 `flash_fwd_sm100.py`）。此时，Python 代码并不会被原生执行。CuTeDSL 框架会拦截 AST，将 Python 语法中的 TMA 描述符配置、Shared Memory 布局（通过 `ampere_helpers.py` 的 Swizzle 逻辑）、以及 `pipeline.py` 中的 `PipelineStateSimple` 状态机实例化为中间表示。

4. **JIT 编译与 MLIR 降级 (JIT & Lowering)**：这是最耗时的一步。CuTeDSL 依赖 `apache-tvm-ffi` 将上述 Python 逻辑降级为 MLIR (Multi-Level Intermediate Representation)。在 MLIR 层，`blackwell_helpers.py` 中的 `tcgen05.mma` 等高级操作被映射为底层的 PTX 内联汇编（如 `llvm.inline_asm`）。随后，编译器生成 PTX 代码。如果你的 Mac 上安装了交叉编译的 `ptxas`（或通过 Mock），它会进一步生成 CUBIN/SASS。

5. **缓存与执行跳过 (Cache & Skip Execution)**：生成的二进制文件被持久化缓存到 `/tmp/${USER}/flash_attention_cute_dsl_cache/`。由于处于 FakeTensor 模式，底层的 CUDA Launch 会被直接 Bypass，测试直接返回 Mock 结果，避免了在 Mac 上调用 CUDA API 导致的崩溃。

6. **静态分析与调优 (Static Analysis - 你的主战场)**：编译完成后，你打开 `AI/` 目录。使用 `AI/parse_clc_log.py` 分析 CLC 调度日志，打开 `AI/SASS_MMA_ANALYSIS.md` 指导你阅读缓存目录下的 PTX/SASS 文件。你纯靠大脑推演寄存器分配（Register Allocation）、检查 TMA Load 是否与 MMA 计算完美掩盖（Latency Hiding）、排查 `barrier.py` 中的 `ld.acquire` 是否存在死锁风险。确认无误后，你才会将代码推送到 CI 或使用 Colab T4 做极短时间的语法/环境连通性验证（注意：T4 无法运行 SM90 代码，最终性能验证必须依赖 CI 的 H100/B200 机器）。

key_types.name: flash_attn_func
key_types.purpose: FA4 的标准注意力机制对外入口，负责参数校验、FakeTensor 拦截和 Kernel 分发。

key_types.name: SchedulerState
key_types.purpose: 调度器状态基类，管理异步流水线 (PipelineAsync) 和生产者/消费者状态 (PipelineState)。

key_types.name: ClcSchedulerState
key_types.purpose: 继承自 SchedulerState，专为 SM90/SM100 的 Cluster Launch Control (CLC) 硬件调度器设计，管理 mbarrier 和响应缓冲区。

key_types.name: PipelineStateSimple
key_types.purpose: 使用单个 Int32 存储 Circular Buffer 的 Index 和 Phase Bit，通过 divmod/位运算实现极低开销的状态推进。

key_types.name: BlackwellFusedMultiHeadAttentionBackwardDKDVKernel
key_types.purpose: SM100 架构下专为 HeadDim=256 设计的反向 dK/dV 计算 Kernel，采用 2-CTA 协同模式以缓解寄存器压力。

key_types.name: FlashPrepareScheduler
key_types.purpose: Varlen (变长序列) 场景下的预处理调度器，计算 cu_seqlens 并生成 Block 级别的任务映射。

key_types.name: gemm_ptx_w_idx
key_types.purpose: 封装 SM100 的底层 MMA 指令，支持直接操作 Tensor Memory (TMEM) 地址进行累加。

key_types.name: ld_acquire
key_types.purpose: 底层同步原语，通过 `llvm.inline_asm` 注入 `ld.global.acquire.gpu.b32` PTX 指令，用于 CTA 间锁获取。

extension_points.how: 接入新模型或新 Attention 变体（如 Sparse MLA）：在此处添加新的 Python 包装函数，处理特定的 Tensor 布局（如 Paged KV Cache），并路由到新的 `@cute.jit` Kernel。
接入新硬件后端（如未来的 SM120）：创建新的 Kernel 文件，并在 `blackwell_helpers.py` 同级创建新的硬件原语封装文件，利用 CuTeDSL 表达新硬件的 TMA/MMA 特性。
接入新调度策略（如 LPT 排序调度）：继承 `SchedulerState`，实现自定义的 Block 坐标计算逻辑，并在 Kernel 初始化时传入新的 Scheduler 实例。

extension_points.where: flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd*.py 中的 Epilogue 阶段
extension_points.how: 接入新算子融合（如 FP8 量化输出）：在 Kernel 的主循环结束后，修改 Epilogue 逻辑，利用 CuTeDSL 的 `cute.copy` 或自定义的数学运算处理 Accumulator 中的数据后再写回 HBM。

hotspots.why: 近期有 34 次提交，是 FA4 (CuTeDSL) 的核心开发区。重点集中在 SM100 架构适配、HD256 优化、Sparse MLA 以及 PackGQA 的谓词（Predication）修复。
近期有 9 次提交，随着 FA4 功能的快速迭代（如 Varlen, Masking, Block Sparsity），测试用例正在被大量补充。这是你验证 FakeTensor 编译的入口。
近期提交热点。SM100 下 HeadDim=256 的反向传播寄存器压力极大，团队正在通过 2-CTA 协同（Cooperative Groups）来拆分 Workload，逻辑极其复杂。
近期提交涉及 Varlen 调度的优化（如 `seqused_q/seqused_k` 支持）。动态调度和 CLC 是打破变长序列负载不均瓶颈的关键。
近期新增的架构设计文档。涉及 Sparse MLA 反向传播中的 In-kernel Recompute-P 技术，这是为了极致节省显存带宽的前沿优化，极具研究价值。

install: export FLASH_ATTENTION_SKIP_CUDA_BUILD="TRUE"  # 核心：跳过 csrc/ 和 hopper/ 目录下遗留 C++/CUDA 代码的编译
conda create -n fa4 python=3.10 -y && conda activate fa4
pip install torch torchvision torchaudio  # 在 Mac 上默认安装 CPU/MPS 版本
pip install nvidia-cutlass-dsl>=4.6.2 einops apache-tvm-ffi quack-kernels>=0.5.3  # 依据 CLAUDE.md 的 FA4 核心依赖
pip install pytest pytest-xdist ruff ninja  # 安装测试、并行与 Lint 工具
pip install -e "flash_attn/cute[dev]"  # 以开发者模式安装 FA4 Python DSL 核心
runbook.no_gpu_paths: 在你的 Mac (Apple Silicon) 上，你可以完整执行 FA4 的「编译期」代码路径。具体包括：`flash_attn/cute/interface.py` (API 路由与 FakeTensor 拦截)、`flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd*.py` 和 `flash_bwd*.py` (CuTeDSL 语法树构建)、以及通过 `apache-tvm-ffi` 触发的底层 JIT 编译过程。最终会在本地生成针对 SM90/SM100 的 PTX 和 CUBIN 文件。你还可以运行 `AI/` 目录下的所有静态分析脚本（如 `parse_clc_log.py`）。你**无法**在 Mac 上执行任何 Kernel 的「运行期」代码。此外，Colab T4 (SM75) 仅能用于验证 `csrc/` 下的 FA2 遗留代码，对 FA4 (强依赖 SM90 TMA/GMMA) 完全无效，只能纯靠阅读代码和 SASS 分析。
smoke_test: FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1 FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1 pytest tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py -k "test_flash_attn_output" -x  # 最小编译冒烟测试
ls -l /tmp/$USER/flash_attention_cute_dsl_cache/  # 验证 PTX/CUBIN 编译产物是否成功落盘
FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1 FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1 pytest tests/cute/test_flash_attn_varlen.py -x  # 验证 Varlen 调度的编译
python AI/parse_clc_log.py --help  # 验证 CLC (Cluster Launch Control) 静态分析工具是否可用
runbook.test_suite: 测试框架为 `pytest`，核心目录在 `tests/cute/`。测试用例通过参数化覆盖了 dtype (fp16/bf16)、headdim (64, 96, 128, 256)、seqlen、causal 以及 MHA/GQA/MQA。针对无 GPU 的 Mac，**必须**使用 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1` 环境变量，这会利用 PyTorch FakeTensorMode 仅传递 Metadata 给编译器而不分配显存。建议使用 `pytest -n 64` (pytest-xdist) 利用 Mac 的多核 CPU 并行编译所有 Kernel。纯编译子集大概耗时在几分钟到十几分钟不等（取决于并发数），执行阶段在 Mac 上会因无 GPU 而跳过或报错。
debug_tips: 环境变量：强依赖 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1` (离线编译) 和 `FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1` (开启编译缓存，极大地加速二次 Debug)。
断点入口：在 `flash_attn/cute/interface.py` 的 `flash_attn_func` 处打断点，观察 PyTorch Tensor 是如何被提取 shape/stride 并转换为 DSL 参数的；在 `flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd.py` 中观察 TMA 描述符的生成逻辑。
静态分析：深度依赖 `AI/` 目录。阅读 `AI/DEBUG_METHODOLOGY.md` 掌握官方 Debug 方法论；使用 `AI/SASS_MMA_ANALYSIS.md` 辅助你在 Mac 上盲看 SASS 指令排布；遇到 Race Condition 怀疑时，参考 `AI/RACECHECK_TMA_HAZARD.md`。
日志开关：关注 `flash_attn/cute/fa_logging.py` 中的日志配置，在编译期打印 CuTeDSL 生成的中间 IR。
runbook.ci: CI 使用 GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/` 和 `tools/ci/`)。根据最近的 Commit 热点，CI 会跑 Wheel 构建（矩阵包含 PyTorch 2.14）以及基于 runner-local SIF (Singularity/Apptainer 容器) 的免注册 GPU 任务。你的 PR 会被以下情况卡住：1. `ruff check flash_attn/cute/` 静态检查失败；2. 在真实的 SM90 (H100) / SM100 机器上运行 `pytest tests/cute/` 时发生精度错误或 TMA 越界（这是你离线盲写最容易踩坑的地方）。
pitfalls: **算力架构幻觉**：试图在 Colab T4 上跑 FA4。FA4 的 `tcgen05.mma` (SM100) 和 TMA/GMMA (SM90) 指令在 T4 (SM75) 上根本不存在，强行运行会导致非法指令错误。你的验证闭环必须在 Mac 上通过 FakeTensor 编译 + SASS 静态分析完成。
**格式化黑洞**：不要对核心 Kernel 文件使用 `ruff format`。根据 `CLAUDE.md`，`flash_bwd.py`, `flash_fwd.py`, `flash_fwd_sm100.py`, `interface.py` 等超大文件被显式排除在自动格式化之外，强行格式化会导致 PR 产生大量无意义的 Diff 并被 Reject。
**遗留代码编译陷阱**：在 Mac 上直接 `python setup.py install` 会触发 `csrc/` 和 `hopper/` 下 C++/CUDA 代码的编译，必然因缺少 NVCC 和 CUDA Toolkit 而报错。必须设置 `FLASH_ATTENTION_SKIP_CUDA_BUILD=TRUE`。
**FakeTensor 遗漏**：在 Mac 上跑 `pytest` 时忘记加 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1`，会导致 PyTorch 尝试初始化 CUDA Context，直接抛出 `AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled`。

community.cadence: 项目处于极度活跃的开发期。根据 Release 记录，FA4 目前保持着严格的每周一个 Beta 版本的高频发布节奏（如 beta29 在 9月2日，beta30 在 9月9日，beta31 在 9月16日）。主分支提交非常频繁，最近一周（2026-09-10 至 09-17）有十余个核心 Commit 合入，且提交热点（Commit Hotspots）高度集中在 `flash_attn/cute`（34次）和 `tests/cute`（9次），这印证了项目正处于向 FA4 (CuTeDSL) 迁移的攻坚阶段。

people.role: 项目创始人 / 核心架构师
people.evidence: README 中的一作，`setup.py` 的 Copyright 所有者，博客 `tridao.me` 的作者，主导了从 FA1 到 FA4 的架构演进。

people.role: 核心维护者
people.evidence: 被指派处理复杂的 Windows 构建问题 (Issue #2832) 以及核心的 head_dim=256/512 架构设计 RFC (Issue #2456)。

people.role: 核心维护者
people.evidence: 与 Johnsonms 共同被指派负责 head_dim=256/512 的 RFC (Issue #2456)，参与核心特性的规划。

community.process: 重大架构变更通常先通过 Issue 提出 RFC（例如 Issue #2456 讨论 head_dim=256/512 的支持）。代码提交前强依赖 `pre-commit` 钩子，根据 `CLAUDE.md` 和 `.pre-commit-config.yaml`，项目使用 `ruff` 进行 lint 和 format，但特别注意大型 Kernel 文件（如 `flash_fwd.py`, `interface.py`）被排除了自动格式化。CI 流程完善，包含 `.github/workflows` 和 `tools/ci`，甚至有针对 GPU 镜像的 registry-free 测试（Commit 1bda8f9）。是否需要 CLA/DCO 需验证。
community.review_style: 极其硬核且结果导向。从 PR 描述（如 PR #2889 明确标出性能提升 `373 → 530 TFLOP/s`）可以看出，Review 极度看重真实的算力利用率（MFU）和底层指令的正确性。对于边界条件（如 padded head dimensions、empty Q/K workloads）的审查非常严格（参考 Commit 0dc2cb4, 008e636）。响应速度极快，多个 PR 在几天内即可完成讨论与合并。
etiquette: 得体：在本地开发时，遵循 `CLAUDE.md` 的规范，将临时脚本、分析日志存放在 `agent_space/` 目录下，避免污染主代码库。
得体：提交 PR 前，利用 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1` 和 `pytest-xdist` (-n) 在本地完成并行的离线编译冒烟测试。
不得体：在 `csrc/` 或 `hopper/` 目录下提交针对新架构（SM90/SM100）的 C++ 代码，目前 FA4 的开发重心已完全转移至 `flash_attn/cute/` 下的 Python CuTeDSL。
不得体：对大型 Kernel 文件（如 `flash_fwd.py`）强行运行全局代码格式化，这会破坏维护者精心排版的矩阵切片与指令对齐逻辑。
what_they_want: SM100 (Blackwell) 架构的极致优化：特别是 Sparse MLA (稀疏注意力) 的反向传播（PR #2893, #2883）以及 Token-pair gather 逻辑。这非常契合你对底层指令推演的能力。
极端 Head Dimension (256, 512) 的支持与调优：这是目前的重点 RFC (#2456)，涉及复杂的寄存器分配与 DSMEM (分布式共享内存) 交换（PR #2889）。你可以通过静态 SASS 分析来帮助优化寄存器溢出问题。
Varlen (变长序列) 的复杂边界 Bug 修复：如处理 packed `split_idx` 导致的死锁 (Issue #2760) 以及非法内存访问 (Issue #2860)。
构建系统的鲁棒性：特别是 Windows 环境下 CUDA 13 的编译问题 (Issue #2832, PR #2872)。

gaps.gap: FA4 (CuTeDSL) 编译产物的自动化静态分析与寄存器溢出（Register Spilling）检测工具不足。
gaps.evidence: 近期 Commit 117d189 专门修复了 'non-causal hdim 128 softmax warps spilling'。`AI/` 目录下虽有 `SASS_MMA_ANALYSIS.md` 和 `parse_clc_log.py`，但缺乏集成到 CI 的自动化 PTX/SASS 寄存器压力分析脚本。
gaps.why_you: 你作为资深 Kernel 工程师，具备极强的底层指令推演能力。在只有 Mac 的情况下，你可以完全通过离线编译生成 PTX，并编写 Python 脚本解析 PTX/SASS，提前发现寄存器溢出，这正是你的核心壁垒。

gaps.gap: 基于 FakeTensor 的极端边界条件（Edge Cases）测试覆盖率仍需完善。
gaps.evidence: 近期 Commit 008e636 修复了 'empty Q/K workloads'，Commit 0dc2cb4 修复了 'padded head dimensions'。这些边界条件在重构为 FA4 时容易被遗漏。
gaps.why_you: 根据 `CLAUDE.md`，FA4 支持 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1`。你可以在 Mac 上无需 GPU 显存，利用 pytest 参数化（如 dtype, seqlen, padding）大规模生成并验证这些边界条件的编译期路由逻辑。

gaps.gap: CuTeDSL 中 Pipeline 状态管理与 Phase Bit 翻转逻辑的抽象存在泄漏或硬编码。
gaps.evidence: `flash_attn/cute/pipeline.py` 中的 `PipelineStateSimple` 依赖手动的位运算（`_phase_index ^= 1`）和 MLIR 值的提取，在复杂的 SM100 2-CTA 调度中容易出错。
gaps.why_you: 你精通 CUDA 异步流水线（TMA/GMMA multi-buffering）。可以在 Mac 上通过阅读 Python DSL 源码，重构和完善 Pipeline 状态机的 Python 侧抽象，并通过比对重构前后的 PTX 产物确保逻辑等价。

gaps.gap: Varlen（变长序列）调度器的元数据构建与验证缺乏纯 CPU 侧的 Mock 测试。
gaps.evidence: `flash_attn/cute/prepare_scheduler.py` 中定义了复杂的 `SchedulerMetadataTensorsTorch`，涉及大量前置的块计算和前缀和（cumsum）逻辑。
gaps.why_you: 这部分逻辑本质上是 CPU/GPU 上的整数路由计算。你可以在 Mac 上编写纯 CPU 的 PyTorch 脚本，Mock 输入的 `cu_seqlens`，验证调度器生成的 block 坐标和 split 数量是否符合预期。

gaps.gap: Sparse MLA (混合注意力) 在 FA4 中的重计算（Recomputation）逻辑与 DSL 表达仍在探索期，缺乏系统性梳理。
gaps.evidence: Commit 294cfb3 刚刚引入了 '[CuTe, SM100] Sparse MLA bwd: in-kernel recompute-P'，且 `AI/` 目录下新增了 `SPARSE_MLA_RECOMPUTE_P.md`。
gaps.why_you: 你擅长扩散模型和 LLM 的稀疏注意力推理加速。可以通过研读该 Markdown 和 DSL 源码，在 Mac 上推演其数学等价性，并帮助完善文档或优化 DSL 循环展开。

gaps.gap: 针对 SM100 (Blackwell) 特有指令（如 tcgen05.mma）的 Python 侧 Intrinsics 封装测试不足。
gaps.evidence: `flash_attn/cute/blackwell_helpers.py` 中封装了大量 `tcgen05` 相关的 MLIR/PTX inline assembly，但缺乏针对这些 helper 函数的独立编译期单元测试。
gaps.why_you: 你可以在 Mac 上编写微型 CuTeDSL kernel，专门调用这些 helper，利用 FakeTensor 触发编译，然后断言生成的 PTX 中是否正确包含了预期的 `tcgen05.mma` 指令及正确的寄存器修饰符。

entry.ownership_target: FA4 CuTeDSL 编译期静态分析与指令级优化基础设施 (Compile-time Static Analysis & Instruction-level Optimization Infrastructure)
entry.why_this_target: 这个方向完美契合你『只有 Mac，无本地 GPU』的硬约束。FA4 的核心范式转移是 JIT 编译，这意味着 Kernel 的正确性（路由、Shape 推导）和性能上限（寄存器压力、TMA 屏障、指令调度）在编译生成 PTX/CUBIN 的那一刻就已经决定了。通过接管 `AI/` 目录下的分析工具链和 FakeTensor 测试框架，你可以在不运行任何真实 GPU 负载的情况下，成为团队中把控 SM90/SM100 Kernel 质量的『守门员』。Tri Dao 和 Johnsonms 等核心维护者在提交真实 GPU 跑分前，将极度依赖你的静态分析工具来排查 SASS 级别的性能瓶颈。这条路径不仅避开了你的硬件劣势，反而放大了你作为资深专家盲写和推演底层指令的绝对优势。
phase_30: 配置 Mac 纯 CPU 开发环境：设置 `export FLASH_ATTENTION_SKIP_CUDA_BUILD="TRUE"`，安装 `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 和 `apache-tvm-ffi`。
跑通编译期冒烟测试：执行 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1 FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1 pytest -n 8 -x tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py`，确保 PTX 成功落盘到 `/tmp`。
精读 API 路由层：深入分析 `flash_attn/cute/interface.py`，理解 PyTorch Tensor 是如何被拦截并提取 Metadata 传递给 CuTeDSL 的。
逆向分析编译产物：挑选一个基础的 SM90 Forward Kernel，对比 `flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm90.py` 源码与生成的 PTX 文件，建立 Python DSL 到 PTX 的心智映射。
研究现有分析工具：运行并阅读 `AI/parse_clc_log.py` 和 `AI/SASS_MMA_ANALYSIS.md`，理解当前团队关注的底层指标。
提交第一个 PR：在 `tests/cute/` 中补充针对近期修复的 Edge Case（如 empty Q/K 或 padded head dim）的 FakeTensor 参数化测试，确保编译期不报错。
phase_60: 开发 PTX 寄存器分析脚本：编写 Python 工具，自动解析 `/tmp` 下生成的 PTX 文件，提取并统计每个 Kernel 的 `maxrregcount`，高亮溢出风险。
分析 SM100 调度器：深入 `flash_attn/cute/tile_scheduler.py` 和 `prepare_scheduler.py`，理解 CLC (Cluster Launch Control) 和动态持久化调度的 Python 侧实现。
提交工具链 PR：将你编写的 PTX 寄存器分析脚本提交到 `AI/` 目录，并在 PR 描述中展示它如何成功复现 Commit 117d189 中的寄存器溢出问题。
优化 DSL 抽象：针对 `flash_attn/cute/pipeline.py` 或 `ampere_helpers.py` 中的冗余逻辑提出重构 PR，通过对比重构前后的 PTX 证明其零开销（Zero-overhead）。
参与架构讨论：在 Issue 区寻找关于 SM100 性能调优或 Sparse MLA 的讨论（如 Issue #2456 类似级别的 RFC），提供基于你静态分析工具的指令级见解。
申请 Triage 权限：在成功合并 2-3 个高质量的测试与工具链 PR 后，向 Tri Dao 申请 Issue Triage 权限，帮助分类 FA4 的编译期 Bug。
phase_90: 集成 CI 静态检查：提交 PR 修改 `.github/workflows`，将你的 PTX 静态分析工具加入 CI 流程。让每个 FA4 的 PR 自动评论其对寄存器数量和 TMA 屏障指令的影响。
主导复杂 Kernel 的离线重构：选择一个复杂的 SM100 Kernel（如 `sm100_hd256_2cta_fmha_backward_dqkernel.py`），通过调整 DSL 循环展开或 Shared Memory 布局来优化指令排布，纯靠 Mac 验证编译产物。
建立 Review 威信：主动 Review 其他贡献者提交到 `flash_attn/cute/` 的 PR。指出其 Python DSL 可能导致的 PTX 膨胀或类型推导错误。
完善 Varlen 调度器测试：为 `prepare_scheduler.py` 贡献一套完整的纯 CPU Mock 测试套件，覆盖各种极端序列长度组合。
申请 Reviewer 身份：凭借在 CI 基础设施、静态分析工具和 CuTeDSL 编译期行为上的深度贡献，正式申请成为 `flash_attn/cute/` 和 `AI/` 目录的 Code Reviewer。

first_prs.title: [Tests] Add parameterized FakeTensor tests for empty Q/K and padded head dimensions in FA4
first_prs.why_safe: 纯 Python 测试代码添加。利用现有的 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1` 机制，不涉及任何真实 GPU 运行。能够有效防止近期 Commit (008e636, 0dc2cb4) 修复的边界问题在后续重构中回归，对项目价值极高且绝对安全。

first_prs.title: [Tools] Add automated PTX register pressure and TMA hazard analyzer
first_prs.why_safe: 这是一个独立的静态分析脚本，完全不影响核心 Kernel 逻辑。它填补了团队在离线性能评估上的空白，且你可以在 Mac 上利用缓存的 PTX 文件进行充分的本地测试和验证。

first_prs.title: [CuTe] Refactor PipelineStateSimple to use explicit bitwise operations for phase management
first_prs.why_safe: 仅修改 Python DSL 侧的抽象表达。你可以通过在 Mac 上离线编译，使用 `diff` 工具对比修改前后生成的 PTX 文件。只要 PTX 完全一致（Bit-exact），这个重构就是 100% 安全的，同时能提升代码可读性。

signals_of_progress: 你的 PR 不再需要你主动解释 '为什么在 Mac 上验证是可靠的'，维护者开始信任你基于 PTX diff 的正确性证明。
Tri Dao 或 Johnsonms 在提交涉及 SM100 核心优化的 PR 时，主动 @ 你，要求你运行静态分析工具查看指令排布是否合理。
你编写的 PTX/SASS 分析脚本被正式集成到 GitHub Actions CI 中，成为 FA4 代码合并的硬性指标（如 maxrregcount 不能超过 128）。
你能够仅通过阅读 `flash_fwd.py` 的 Python 代码，就能在脑海中准确映射出对应的 TMA load 和 GMMA math 指令序列。

risks.risk: 盲目进行 DSL 优化导致真实 GPU 上的性能回退（如 Cache Miss 增加），因为静态分析无法完全模拟动态访存行为。
risks.mitigation: 在提交涉及性能优化的 PR 时，明确标注 'Verified via PTX static analysis only'。主动在 PR 中请求拥有 H100/B200 的维护者（如 Johnsonms）帮忙运行 `benchmarks/bench_sm90.py` 并贴出 MFU 结果后再合并。

risks.risk: Mac (Apple Silicon) 上的 `apache-tvm-ffi` 或 `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 依赖出现跨平台兼容性问题，导致无法生成 PTX。
risks.mitigation: 如果 ARM64 原生环境受限，准备一个基于 Rosetta 2 的 x86_64 Conda 环境，或者使用轻量级的 Linux Docker 容器在 Mac 上运行编译流程。

risks.risk: 对 SM100 (Blackwell) 的全新指令集（如 tcgen05.mma, TMA multicast）理解出现偏差，导致静态分析工具给出错误建议。
risks.mitigation: 深入研读 `flash_attn/cute/blackwell_helpers.py` 中的 MLIR inline assembly，并交叉对比 NVIDIA 官方的 PTX ISA 文档。遇到不确定的指令行为，在 Issue 中向团队虚心请教确认。

risks.risk: 长期无法接触真实硬件，导致对项目的参与感降低，陷入纯粹的 '纸上谈兵' 带来的倦怠。
risks.mitigation: 将成就感建立在 '工具链的被使用率' 上。当看到你的 CI 拦截了一个会导致真实 GPU 性能下降 20% 的 Bad Commit 时，这就是你作为架构师的最大价值。同时，可以利用 Colab T4 偶尔跑一下 FA2 的遗留代码保持手感。

issues.title: Windows build fails with CUDA 13.4: missing /Zc:preprocessor, /std:c++17 pinned (plus no sm_121 gencode)
issues.body:
Hi! I tried building 2.8.4 from source on Windows and hit some failures, all in setup.py's Windows branch. They're build configuration only - no kernel, CUTLASS or host-code changes required. I have them all fixed locally and can open a PR. The README says Windows "might work starting v2.3.2 ... but Windows compilation still requires more testing" and invites people to open an issue, so here it is.

Environment: Windows 11 ARM64, MSVC 14.51 (ARM64 host and target), CUDA 13.4, torch 2.15, CPython 3.13 and 3.14, sm_121 (GB10).

The three things that go wrong, all in build configuration rather than the kernels:

**1. There's no `sm_121` gencode.** `cuda_archs()` defaults to `"80;90;100;110;120"` and
`add_cuda_gencodes()` has no `121` branch, so nothing gets emitted for this GPU.

**2. CUDA 13.x's CCCL headers refuse MSVC's traditional preprocessor.** Every `.cu` stops
here:

```
cccl/cuda/std/__cccl/preprocessor.h(20): fatal error C1189: #error: MSVC/cl.exe with
traditional preprocessor is used ... pass `/Zc:preprocessor` to cl.exe
```

The Windows branch passes `/Zc:__cplusplus` already, just not `/Zc:preprocessor`.

**3. `/std:c++17` is pinned, and torch 2.15's headers need C++20:**

```
c10/util/StringUtil.h(171): error C7555: use of designated initializers requires at
  least '/std:c++20'
c10/util/intrusive_ptr.h(775): error C2039: 'strong_ordering': is not a member of 'std'
```

(There's also `M_LOG2E` in `src/softmax.h(76)` coming up undefined, which MSVC only
provides with `_USE_MATH_DEFINES`.)

One thing that might matter more than the ARM64 angle: only (1) is actually
architecture-specific. (2) and (3) look like they'd hit Windows x64 with the same CUDA and
torch versions just as hard.

issues.title: [CuTe, SM80] Forward silently ignores `block_sparse_tensors` and returns dense attention
issues.body:
## Problem

On SM80-class GPUs, calling `flash_attn_func(..., block_sparse_tensors=...)` ignores the block sparse configuration entirely. 
The kernel computes dense attention and returns it without any error or warning, so the caller believes they got a sparse result when they did not.

## Reproduction

Environment: RTX A6000 (SM86), torch 2.14.0+cu130, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, main @ 1bda8f9

Configure every Q block to attend only to KV block 0 (all full blocks, no `mask_mod` needed),
then compare against PyTorch dense / sparse references:

```python
import torch, math
from flash_attn.cute import flash_attn_func
from flash_attn.cute.block_sparsity import BlockSparseTensorsTorch

torch.manual_seed(0)
B, S, H, D = 1, 512, 2, 64
q, k, v = [torch.randn(B, S, H, D, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16) for _ in range(3)]
M, N = S // 128, S // 64
bst = BlockSparseTensorsTorch(
    mask_block_cnt=torch.zeros(B, H, M, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    mask_block_idx=torch.zeros(B, H, M, N, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    full_block_cnt=torch.ones(B, H, M, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    full_block_idx=torch.zeros(B, H, M, N, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    block_size=(128, 64),
)
out, lse = flash_attn_func(q, k, v, block_sparse_tensors=bst, return_lse=True)

qt, kt, vt = [x.float().transpose(1, 2) for x in (q, k, v)]
keep = torch.zeros(S, S, dtype=torch.bool, device="cuda"); keep[:, :64] = True
dense = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(qt, kt, vt).transpose(1, 2)
sparse = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(qt, kt, vt, attn_mask=keep).transpose(1, 2)
print("vs dense :", (out.float() - dense).abs().max().item())
print("vs sparse:", (out.float() - sparse).abs().max().item())
```

Output:

```
vs dense : 0.00014
vs sparse: 0.95
```

## Expected behavior

Either honor the block sparse configuration, or raise an explicit error.

## Cause

- The SM80 branch in `interface.py` (`arch // 10 == 8`) only asserts that paged KV and SplitKV are unsupported. Unlike the SM120 branch, it has no `assert not use_block_sparsity`.
- `FlashAttentionForwardSm80.__call__` accepts a `blocksparse_tensors` argument, but the function body never uses it.

## Suggested fix

The minimal fix is to add the following to the SM80 branch:

```python
assert not use_block_sparsity, "Block sparsity not supported on SM 8.0"
```

I am happy to submit a PR for this if the maintainers agree. 
Whether to actually implement block sparsity in the SM80 kernel is a separate discussion.

issues.title: Support head_dim=512 on SM89 (Ada) for Gemma 4 global attention layers
issues.body:
## Feature request

Add a `head_dim=512` forward path in FlashAttention for **compute capability 8.9 (Ada — L40, L40S, RTX 4090)**.

## Why

Google's Gemma 4 ships a hybrid attention design with 4 global-attention layers at `head_dim=512` (alongside 26 layers at `head_dim=256`, which FA2 already handles cleanly). On SM89, `flash_attn_varlen_func` currently rejects `head_dim=512` outright — the model can't use FlashAttention for those layers at all.

## Why a separate ask from #2427

#2427 tracks `head_dim=512` generically. The path being explored there is **FA4 / cute** kernels, which depend on Hopper TMA + WGMMA. FA3 and FA4 are gated to compute capability ≥ 8 **excluding 8.6 and 8.9**, so anything that lands in FA4 will not reach Ada GPUs.

For SM89 the realistic path is **extending FA2** (or a dedicated SM89 kernel) to handle `head_dim=512`. We understand this is harder:
- No TMA — global→shared loads have to be hand-staged.
- No WGMMA — smaller MMA tiles → tighter SMEM budget for a 512-wide head.

## What would be sufficient

A `head_dim=512` forward path (varlen + paged-KV) on SM89, FP16/BF16 Q/K/V, with FP8 KV-cache support if feasible. Prefill is the more painful case for long-context Gemma 4 inference; decode is a bonus. Causal-mask + sliding-window support to match the rest of FA2.

issues.title: [FA4/B200] return_lse=True makes D64 forward about 19% faster
issues.body:
I had my agent create this reproducer while doing some heuristic tuning. This is quite strange, and I wanted to track it.

On B200, the FA4 CuTe forward kernel for dense BF16 attention with `(B, S, H, D) = (2, 16384, 16, 64)` is consistently faster when `return_lse=True`, even though that specialization calculates and writes the additional LSE output.


### Agent notes

## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA B200 (SM100)
- PyTorch: `2.14.0.dev20260722+cu132`
- PyTorch CUDA runtime: 13.2
- NVIDIA CuTe DSL: `4.6.0.dev0`
- FlashAttention commit: `00756db9d921da0846453283ddfbeb7457abd09b`
- Dtype: BF16
- Causal: false
- Measurement: fixed-pointer CUDA graph replay, 25 warmups and 100 measured replays per round, five alternating A/B rounds

## Result

```text
GPU: NVIDIA B200
Torch: 2.14.0.dev20260722+cu132 (CUDA 13.2)
CuTe DSL: 4.6.0.dev0
FA4 commit: 00756db9d921da0846453283ddfbeb7457abd09b
no-LSE: median=3.0018 ms rounds=[3.007457275390625, 3.0017739868164064, 3.001456604003906, 3.0028912353515627, 3.0008636474609376]
with-LSE: median=2.5281 ms rounds=[2.5091484069824217, 2.545796203613281, 2.512978210449219, 2.5281126403808596, 2.532301177978516]
with-LSE speedup: 1.187x
```

Both paths pass a correctness check against PyTorch SDPA.

A focused Nsight Compute comparison showed the same launch topology and resource limits for both specializations (148 blocks, 512 threads, 128 registers/thread, and approximately 232 KB dynamic shared memory). The no-LSE specialization had substantially fewer eligible/issued warps and more samples around the pipeline synchronization path. This looks more like a compiler scheduling/code-generation cliff than an inherent benefit from calculating LSE.

I have only established this behavior on B200; this report does not claim the same result on GB300.

## Minimal reproducer

Run with:

```bash
python repro_fa4_lse_b200.py /path/to/flash-attention
```

```python
"""Reproduce the FA4 D64 B200 performance inversion caused by returning LSE."""

import argparse
import importlib
import importlib.metadata
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path
from types import ModuleType
from typing import Callable

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def load_fa4_interface(fa4_root: Path) -> ModuleType:
    """Load the CuTe FA4 interface without requiring the FA2 extension."""
    package = ModuleType("flash_attn")
    package.__path__ = [str(fa4_root / "flash_attn")]
    sys.modules["flash_attn"] = package
    return importlib.import_module("flash_attn.cute.interface")


def make_call(
    interface: ModuleType,
    q: torch.Tensor,
    k: torch.Tensor,
    v: torch.Tensor,
    return_lse: bool,
) -> Callable[[], torch.Tensor]:
    """Create one allocation-free FA4 forward specialization."""
    out = torch.empty_like(q)
    lse = (
        torch.empty(q.shape[0], q.shape[2], q.shape[1], device=q.device)
        if return_lse
        else None
    )

    def run() -> torch.Tensor:
        return interface._flash_attn_fwd(
            q, k, v, out=out, lse=lse, return_lse=return_lse
        )[0]

    return run


def capture(function: Callable[[], torch.Tensor]) -> torch.cuda.CUDAGraph:
    """Capture a warmed FA4 call into a fixed-pointer CUDA graph."""
    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
        for _ in range(3):
            function()
    stream.synchronize()

    wit

issues.body:
## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 6000D 84 GB (sm_120, GeForce Blackwell), driver 595.84, CUDA 13.2
- flash-attn-4: 4.0.0b26 and 4.0.0b29 (both tested)
- nvidia-cutlass-dsl: 4.6.0.dev0 / 4.6.2 / 4.7.1 (all three tested)
- torch 2.13.0+cu129, torchvision 0.28.0, Python 3.12
- Workload: MiniMax-H3 hybrid-attention video model (VDN-MiniMax-H3) — bf16 packed
  varlen attention, H=56 heads, D=128, per-window varlen segments
  (q ~5040 rows/segment, kv ~17580 rows/segment), called once per DiT block per NFE.

## Summary

Two independent problems when running FA4 on SM120:

1. **`AuxData` cannot cross the CuTe-DSL JIT boundary** — the SM120 forward path
   (`FlashAttentionForwardSm120`) passes `AuxData(cute_aux_tensors, aux_scalars)` as
   positional arg #17, but the DSL has no adapter for this NamedTuple
   (`JitArgAdapterRegistry.default_dataclass_adapter` is never registered in a plain
   `flash_attn_func`/`flash_attn_varlen_func` install, and NamedTuples are not
   auto-adapted). Consequences differ by DSL version:
   - DSL 4.6.2: `CUDADialectError` (empty message) → clean failure, kernel never runs
   - DSL 4.6.0.dev0 / 4.7.1: only a `UserWarning` ("cannot be converted to a
     JitArgument ... implement the JitArgument protocol"), then the kernel is
     launched with a mangled argument → **illegal memory access**

   Workaround that makes the kernel compile and run (register a zero-width
   JitArgument adapter; our calls always have `tensors=None, scalars=None`, at which
   point the kernel body early-returns in `compute_fastdiv_mods`):

   ```python
   import flash_attn.cute.utils as fa_utils
   import cutlass  # canonical DSL import path
   from cutlass.base_dsl.runtime.jit_arg_adapters import JitArgAdapterRegistry

   class _ZeroWidthAux:
       def __init__(self, src): self._src = src
       def __getattr__(self, name): return getattr(self._src, name)
       def __get_mlir_types__(self): return []
       def __c_pointers__(self): return []
       def __new_from_mlir_values__(self, values): return self

   def _adapt(aux):
       if aux.tensors is None and aux.scalars is None:
           return _ZeroWidthAux(aux)
       raise NotImplementedError("non-empty AuxData")

   JitArgAdapterRegistry.register_jit_arg_adapter(fa_utils.AuxData)(_adapt)
   ```

   Suggested upstream fixes (either): register a default dataclass/NamedTuple
   adapter in `base_dsl` when `default_dataclass_adapter` is unset, or annotate/
   adapt `AuxData` in `interface.py` so `flash_attn_func`/`flash_attn_varlen_func`
   work out of the box on SM120.

2. **With (1) worked around, the SM120 kernel still hits an illegal memory access
   once the varlen batch has >= 4 segments under real-workload memory layouts.**
   Details below. This is the blocker: the kernel is ~7x faster than our fallback
   for small inputs, but cannot be used for real renders.

Bisect over sequence length (same call, same shapes family, real model):

issues.body:
### Summary

On B300/SM103, FA4 beta27's backward preprocess reuses a predicate covering all per-thread row modes after slicing the O/dO source and destination tensors to a single row. CuTe rejects the resulting copy because the predicate has shape `(1,(2,3))` while the data expects `(1,(3))`.

The same `flash_bwd_preprocess.py` code is present in beta29 and current `main` (`4fd8d758c1fb7d93ef2e9a316ba4db1ab7fc05fe` as fetched on 2026-09-03).

### Environment

- NVIDIA B300 / SM103
- CUDA 13.2 base image
- PyTorch 2.10.0a0+3a035ad5.nv25.12
- Python 3.13
- `flash-attn-4==4.0.0b27`
- `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.2`
- BF16, varlen causal attention
- `CUTE_DSL_SHOW_STACKTRACE=1`

### Sanitized reproducer

```python
import torch
from flash_attn.cute import flash_attn_varlen_func

torch.manual_seed(42)
q = torch.randn(256, 16, 80, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
k = torch.randn(256, 4, 80, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
v = torch.randn(256, 4, 80, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
cu = torch.tensor([0, 256], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
result = flash_attn_varlen_func(
    q,
    k,
    v,
    cu_seqlens_q=cu,
    cu_seqlens_k=cu,
    max_seqlen_q=256,
    max_seqlen_k=256,
    causal=True,
)
out = result[0] if isinstance(result, tuple) else result
out.float().square().mean().backward()
```

Backward-preprocess compile key:

```text
dtype=BFloat16, head_dim=80, head_dim_v=80, m_block_size=128,
has_cuseqlens_q=True, has_seqused_q=False, has_dlse=False,
has_dq_accum=True, has_scale_p=False, use_padded_offsets=True,
nheads_major=False, pack_gqa=False, qhead_per_kvhead=1,
nheads_kv=1, has_cu_total_m_blocks=False
```

Compiler diagnostic:

```text
error: unknown: 'cute.copy' op expects pred to have compatible shape with: (1,(3)) but got actual predShape: (1,(2,3))
note: unknown: see current operation: "cute.copy"(...) :
  (!cute_nvgpu.atom.universal_copy<bf16, 128 b>,
   !cute.memref<bf16, gmem, align<16>, "((8,1),(3)):((1,0),(32))">,
   !cute.memref<bf16, rmem, align<16>, "((8,1),(3)):((1,0),(8))">,
   !cute.memref<i8, rmem, align<32>, "(1,(2,3)):(3,(0,1))">) -> ()
```

### Source mapping and proposed correction

`flash_attn/cute/flash_bwd_preprocess.py` constructs `tOpO` from unsliced `tOcO`, then captures it in a `partial`. Inside the `m` loop it slices both data tensors with `[None, m, None]` but does not slice the predicate.

Slicing the predicate over the same row mode makes the preprocess compile and run:

```diff
-copy = partial(copy_utils.copy, pred=tOpO)
 ...
-copy(tOgO[None, m, None], tOrO[None, m, None])
-copy(tOgdO[None, m, None], tOrdO[None, m, None])
+row_predicate = tOpO[None, m, None] if const_expr(tOpO is not None) else None
+copy_utils.copy(tOgO[None, m, None], tOrO[None, m, None], pred=row_predicate)
+copy_utils.copy(tOgdO[None, m, None], tOrdO[None, m, None], pred=row_predicate)
```

This report is limited to the backward-preprocess predicate mismatch; the reproducer may encounter other constraints later in the general SM100 backward kernel once preprocess is repaired.

issues.title: splitkv early-exit path ignores unpadded_lse, writing -inf to the wrong LSE slot
issues.body:
**Title:** splitkv early-exit path ignores `unpadded_lse`, writing `-inf` to the wrong LSE slot

**Repo:** Dao-AILab/flash-attention (also present in the vllm-project fork)

---

`flash_fwd_splitkv_kernel` computes the LSE write offset two different ways depending on
which exit it takes, and only one of them honours `params.unpadded_lse`.

**Normal exit** — `csrc/flash_attn/src/flash_fwd_kernel.h:1030`:

```cpp
const index_t row_offset_lseaccum = (Split || !params.unpadded_lse ?
        ((n_split_idx * params.b + bidb) * params.h + bidh) * params.seqlen_q
      : bidh * params.total_q + binfo.q_offset(params.seqlen_q, 1, bidb)
    ) + m_block * kBlockM;
```

**Early exit** (taken when `n_block_max <= n_block_min`, e.g. a zero-length or fully-masked
KV sequence) — `flash_fwd_kernel.h:552`:

```cpp
const index_t row_offset_lseaccum = ((n_split_idx * params.b + bidb) * params.h + bidh) * params.seqlen_q
    + m_block * kBlockM;
```

The ternary is missing. So when `unpadded_lse` is set and `Split` is false, the early exit
writes `-inf` into `params.softmax_lse_ptr` at a **dense** `(b, h, seqlen_q)` offset, while
the buffer is laid out **unpadded** as `(h, total_q)`. The two offsets coincide only when
`b == 1` and `seqlen_q == total_q`.

**Effect:** a varlen batch containing a zero-length (or fully masked) KV sequence writes
`-inf` into a different sequence's LSE slot, or out of bounds. `unpadded_lse` is set on the
varlen path, so any caller passing `return_softmax_lse=True` with a mixed batch is exposed.

**Why it is rarely seen:** early-exit CTAs finish almost immediately, so in practice the
correct value is usually written afterwards by the CTA that owns the slot, masking the race.
It is a genuine wrong-address write regardless of who wins.

**Fix:** apply the same ternary at `:552` as at `:1030`.

**Found while** validating a split-k change to `mha_varlen_fwd` in the vllm-project fork; this
bug is independent of that change and predates it. With split-k engaged the `-inf` is routed
correctly through the combine kernel, so the patched path does not hit it — this is about the
unsplit path.

**Not tested by:** the current suite never constructs a zero-length KV sequence in a varlen
batch with `return_softmax_lse=True`.

issues.title: Using `torch.library.wrap_triton` introduces measurable CPU overhead in `rotary`
issues.body:
older releases such as 2.7.4 don't do this
```
AFFECTED PATTERN: flash-attn 2.8.3.post1 rotary uses bare wrap_triton
installed path:    89.97 us/call
direct bypass:     19.97 us/call
recoverable:       70.00 us/call (4.5x)
```
minimal repro:
```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal reproducer for eager torch.library.wrap_triton overhead."""

import statistics
import time
import inspect

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def touch(x):
    tl.store(x, 0.0)


x = torch.empty(1, device="cuda")
raw = touch
wrapped = torch.library.wrap_triton(touch)  # Cache it: construction is not the issue.
grid = lambda meta: (1,)  # Match the callable-grid path used by FlashAttention.


def time_calls(fn, calls=1000, repeats=7):
    fn()  # Compile/warm up outside the measurement.
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    samples = []
    for _ in range(repeats):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(calls):
            fn()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        samples.append((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1e6 / calls)
    return statistics.median(samples)


raw_us = time_calls(lambda: raw[grid](x))
wrapped_us = time_calls(lambda: wrapped[grid](x))
print(f"raw:     {raw_us:8.2f} us/launch")
print(f"wrapped: {wrapped_us:8.2f} us/launch")
print(f"overhead:{wrapped_us - raw_us:8.2f} us/launch ({wrapped_us / raw_us:.1f}x)")


print("\nInstalled FlashAttention check:")
try:
    import flash_attn
    from flash_attn.ops.triton import rotary
except ImportError as error:
    print(f"SKIP: FlashAttention is not importable ({error})")
else:
    version = getattr(flash_attn, "__version__", "unknown")
    source = inspect.getsource(rotary.apply_rotary)
    if "torch.library.wrap_triton" not in source:
        print(f"UNAFFECTED: flash-attn {version} rotary does not use bare wrap_triton")
    else:
        print(f"AFFECTED PATTERN: flash-attn {version} rotary uses bare wrap_triton")
    q = torch.ones((1, 1, 1, 2), device="cuda")
    cos = torch.ones((1, 1), device="cuda")
    sin = torch.zeros((1, 1), device="cuda")
    call = lambda: rotary.apply_rotary(q, cos, sin, inplace=True)
    native_us = time_calls(call, calls=500, repeats=5)
    original_wrap_triton = torch.library.wrap_triton
    try:
        torch.library.wrap_triton = lambda kernel: kernel
        direct_us = time_calls(call, calls=500, repeats=5)
    finally:
        torch.library.wrap_triton = original_wrap_triton
    print(f"installed path: {native_us:8.2f} us/call")
    print(f"direct bypass:  {direct_us:8.2f} us/call")
    print(f"recoverable:    {native_us - direct_us:8.2f} us/call ({native_us / direct_us:.1f}x)")
```

issues.title: [FA4] max_seqlen_q tensor causes an argument-annotation mismatch in varlen forward
issues.body:
## Summary

The FA4 varlen forward path can pass a scalar `torch.Tensor` for `max_seqlen_q` into `cute.compile()`, while the compiled function declares that parameter as `Int32 | int | None`. This makes compilation fail with an argument-annotation mismatch.

## Reproduction

From a checkout of the current default branch, run:

```bash
pytest tests/cute/test_flash_attn_fast.py -k test_flash_attn_varlen_tensor_max_seqlen_reuses_fwd_cache
```

## Actual behavior

The test fails with an error equivalent to:

```
expects argument #26 (max_seqlen_q) to be one of (Int32, int, NoneType), but got torch.Tensor
```

## Expected behavior

The cache-stabilization path should retain its intended behavior while passing a value consistent with the compiled function's type contract.

## Possible direction

Normalize the scalar before invoking `cute.compile()` (for example, construct the appropriate CUTLASS DSL scalar type), or update the relevant API contract if a tensor is the intended representation.

issues.title: Flash Attention install with Triton backend replaces preinstalled Triton no matter what.
issues.body:
Some context here, my GPU is an AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700. This GPU requires a specific build of Triton (currently, triton-3.7.0+git1bff1d9d.rocm7.13.0a20260416 from https://rocm.nightlies.amd.com/v2/gfx120X-all/) for use with ComfyUI. The problem is that Flash Attention quietly (atleast in the command stdout) pulls AITER as a git submodule in the setup.py, the default build of which will replace your preinstalled Triton with "3.7.1". I would recommend passing "AITER_USE_SYSTEM_TRITON=1" to the AITER build if Triton is detected as already being installed.

I believe the relevant code in setup.py is this: (although I may be wrong)
```python
if ROCM_BACKEND == "triton":
        if os.path.isdir(".git"):
            subprocess.run(["git", "submodule", "update", "--init", "third_party/aiter"], check=True)
        else:
            assert os.path.isdir("third_party/aiter"), (
                "third_party/aiter is missing, please use source distribution or git clone"
            )
        subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "--no-build-isolation", "third_party/aiter"],
            check=True,
        )
```

Steps to recreate:
1. Install any Triton version besides 3.7.1.
2. Run the recommended command: `FLASH_ATTENTION_TRITON_AMD_ENABLE="TRUE" pip install --no-build-isolation .`
3. Check the current Triton version. (`pip list | grep triton` or similar command)

## Summary

I am seeing unexpectedly poor backward performance from the ROCm CK backend of FlashAttention on an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (gfx1201, RDNA4) on Windows.

Forward performance is good and consistently faster than PyTorch SDPA, but backward is **4.4x to 7.4x slower** than SDPA, with the gap increasing at longer sequence lengths. Forward + backward is therefore **3.3x to 6.0x slower** than SDPA.

Numerical results look correct, so this appears to be a performance issue rather than a correctness issue.

This resembles the old ROCm FlashAttention backward performance issue:
https://github.com/ROCm/flash-attention/issues/44

That issue was eventually reported as fixed after the ck_tile refactor. I am wondering whether the gfx1201 / RDNA4 backward path is hitting an untuned or fallback CK kernel.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Pro
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT
- Architecture: gfx1201
- PyTorch: `2.15.0a0+rocm10.1.0a20260814`
- HIP: `7.16.26323`
- FlashAttention source tag: `fa4-v4.0.0.beta26`

dQ relative L2: 1.489228e-03

issues.title: FA4 backward does not return against cutlass-dsl 4.6.0 and 4.6.1 on B300 (sm_103)
issues.body:
On a B300 (sm_103), FA4's backward stops returning when the loaded CuTe DSL runtime is 4.6.0 or 4.6.1. The pinned prerelease and the current release are both fine.

| nvidia-cutlass-dsl runtime | dense backward | varlen backward |
|---|---|---|
| 4.6.0.dev0 (the pin) | completes | completes |
| 4.6.0 | no return in 180s | completes |
| 4.6.1 | no return in 180s | completes |
| 4.6.2 | completes | completes |

Three runs per cell, and two per cell in a separate environment built from scratch with an independently written test, agreeing cell for cell.

Setup: flash-attn-4 4.0.0b26, torch 2.14.0.dev20260806+cu130, CUDA 13.0. Each run in its own process under an external timeout, since the kernel never returns. Dense goes through SDPA with the FA4 impl active, bf16, B=2 H=4 S=256 D=64, non-causal. Varlen goes through `torch.nn.attention.varlen.varlen_attn`, four segments of 256, 4 heads, head dim 64. The stall is inside `_bwd_postprocess_convert`, with the same stack sampled 75 seconds apart. With grouped-query attention the varlen path stops too — 16 query heads against 8 key/value heads is enough.

Two things about how this stayed hidden, which may be more useful than the table.

The pin moved from `>=4.5.2` to `==4.6.0.dev0` in #2648 on 2026-06-25, and 4.6.0 was released on 07-02 — so no released runtime has been inside the declared range since. The pin also excludes 4.6.2, while `quack-kernels` 0.6.4 requires exactly 4.6.2, so an environment holding both cannot satisfy them.

And the version does not tell you what is loaded. `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` is a meta-package whose runtime ships in `-libs-cu12` and `-libs-cu13`; a process loads one. An environment can report 4.6.2 from `importlib.metadata` while loading a cu13 runtime still at 4.6.0 — which happens when something else pins the cu13 extra, as vllm does with `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.6.0`. The reproduction below prints the mapped library for that reason.

Is 4.6.2 intended to work? If so, would you consider widening the pin?

Possibly the same thing, untested from here: #2466 (FA4 with softcap hangs on backward).

## Reproduction

```bash
pip install "flash-attn-4==4.0.0b26" --no-deps
pip install "nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.0" "quack-kernels>=0.5.3" "apache-tvm-ffi>=0.1.12,<0.2"

timeout 180 python repro.py     # reaches BACKWARD_DONE
```

issues.title: publish.yml: create trigger has no tag filter, so branch pushes fail the workflow and new matrix entries never build
issues.body:
## Summary

`.github/workflows/publish.yml` triggers on:

```yaml
on:
  create:
    tags:
      - v*
```

The `create` event does not support filters, so the `tags:` key is silently ignored and the workflow also fires on **branch** creation. `setup_release` then runs:

```bash
gh release create ${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/} --repo $GITHUB_REPOSITORY --title ... --generate-notes
```

For a branch, `refs/heads/...` does not match the `refs/tags/` prefix, so the ref is passed through unstripped and the step fails:

```
HTTP 422: Validation Failed (https://api.github.com/repos/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/releases)
pre_receive Sorry, branch or tag names starting with 'refs/' are not allowed.
Published releases must have a valid tag
```

`build_wheels` and `publish_package` are `needs:`-dependent, so both are skipped.

## Impact

Almost every run of "Build wheels and deploy" is a failure triggered by an ordinary branch push — e.g. [run 31060582771](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/actions/runs/31060582771) on `refs/heads/drisspg/stack/60`. Of the last 100 runs, 99 are branch refs (95 failed, 4 cancelled) and the single success is the tag run `v2.8.3.post1`. The real signal is buried in that noise.

Worth noting the compute cost is near zero — every one of those runs dies in `setup_release` within seconds and the matrix never starts. The cost is signal: the workflow reads as permanently broken, and a genuine release failure would be indistinguishable from the background.

## A separate problem: the current matrix has never run

This is **not** caused by the trigger bug, and I want to be precise about that since the two are easy to conflate. The tag path works correctly under `create` — [run 27279915131](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/actions/runs/27279915131) is the `v2.8.3.post1` run and it succeeded and published.

A tag-triggered run uses the workflow *as it exists at that tag*, and `v2.8.3.post1` points at a commit off a line that diverged from `main` well before the matrix was updated:

```
v2.8.3.post1...main      status: diverged, ahead_by 558, behind_by 2
v2.8.3.post1...c04a808   status: diverged, ahead_by 357, behind_by 2
```

So c04a808 (adds torch 2.9.1 / 2.10.0 and CUDA 13) is not in the tag's tree. Reading `publish.yml` at the tag confirms it still carries `python-version: ['3.9' … '3.13']` and `torch-version: ['2.4.0' … '2.8.0']` — which is why the newest tag has *older* torch coverage than `main` declares.

The practical consequence: fixing the trigger does not by itself build any wheels, and a tag cut from current `main` would run the current matrix with or without the trigger fix. Both changes are worth making; neither substitutes for the other.

Net result today: no cp310 / cp311 / cp313 wheels exist for torch >= 2.9. The only ones published are cp312 — five on `v2.8.3` (uploaded 2025-12-17, 2026-06-02, 2026-06-11, 2026-06-12) and two on `v2.8.3.post1` (2026-06-11) — and those scattered individual timestamps suggest they were added by hand rather than by a matrix run.

## Suggested fix

Move to a trigger that supports filtering:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'
```

`publish-fa4.yml` already uses exactly this form (with `fa4-v*`), and the globs do not collide since the pattern is anchored at the start.

Gating the first job instead would also stop the failures:

```yaml
jobs:
  setup_release:
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')
```

but it is the weaker option — it still creates a workfl

issues.title: ops/triton/linear.py kernel_fwd computes its bounds mask and never passes it to the store
issues.body:
## Summary

`kernel_fwd` builds exactly the bounds mask its output store needs, on the line directly above the store, and then calls `tl.store(C, acc)` without it. The host grid rounds up with `cdiv`, so whenever `M` or `N` is not a multiple of the autotuned block sizes the last tiles write their full `BLOCK_M × BLOCK_N` extent: past the end of the `(M, N)` output allocation, and — because an N-tail overshoot lands on the next row of the same tensor — onto cells owned by other tiles, so the in-bounds output is also wrong, nondeterministically. The sibling `kernel_bwd` in the same file has the identical three lines and stores with `mask=mask`.

This reaches users through `triton_linear_act` / `FusedDenseSqreluDense` (`flash_attn/ops/triton/mlp.py`). Two scoping notes: tile-aligned shapes (powers of two) hide the bug completely, which is why tests and benchmarks never see it; and the module imports `triton.ops.matmul_perf_model`, which no longer exists in triton ≥ 3.0 — so the affected code is usable (and broken) only on triton 2.x builds (torch ≤ 2.3).

## Reproduction

```python
import torch
from flash_attn.ops.triton.linear import triton_linear_act

torch.manual_seed(0)
M, N, K = 513, 1000, 256
x = torch.randn(M, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
w = torch.randn(N, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
ref = (x.float() @ w.float().t()).half()
for _ in range(3):
    out = triton_linear_act(x, w)
    print(int((~torch.isclose(out, ref, atol=1e-1, rtol=1e-1)).sum()), "wrong cells of", M * N)
```

Output at a369df7 (L40S, torch 2.3.1 / triton 2.3.1):

```
[M=513 N=1000 K=256] wrong output cells vs x @ w.T over 3 runs: [6472, 6113, 10358] of 513000
[M=512 N=1024 K=256 (tile-aligned control)] wrong output cells: [0, 0, 0]
```

The varying counts across identical runs are the tile race on the in-bounds cells; under `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` (with `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`) a single small call at M=5, N=17, K=9 reports invalid global writes attributed to the store at `linear.py:255` and then ends in an unspecified launch failure, and passing the mask that is already computed there gives 0 wrong cells, deterministic, and 0 sanitizer errors.

## Environment

- flash-attention commit a369df7 (main); flash_attn 2.7.4.post1 wheel for the compiled extension, checkout sources for the Triton module
- NVIDIA L40S (sm_89), driver CUDA 12.4
- torch 2.3.1+cu121, triton 2.3.1, Python 3.10

issues.title: [CuTe, SM100] test_clc_fuzz fails after #2559 due to stale scheduler expectations
issues.body:
## Summary

After #2559, `tests/cute/test_clc_fuzz.py` fails on SM100 because several scheduler-class assertions still reflect the scheduler dispatch behavior from before #2559.

At commit `c68c592fd9da1e40a4fb0b56229caae6754ac5c9`, the test result is:

```text
22 failed, 167 passed
```

## Representative failures:
```text
AssertionError: Expected SingleTileVarlenScheduler, got StaticPersistentTileScheduler

AssertionError: Expected SingleTileVarlenScheduler, got DynamicPersistentVarlenScheduler

AssertionError: Expected SingleTileScheduler fallback, got StaticPersistentTileScheduler
```
Current main (1cc7ff67cbc5685046c75183e8defecca3e35d5c) still contains the same assertions.
## Reproduction
On an SM100 GPU:
```
pytest -n=16 --tb=short tests/cute/test_clc_fuzz.py
```
Environment used for the observed failure:
GPU: GB200/B200, SM100
OS: Ubuntu 24.04, arm64
Python: 3.12.8
CUDA: 13.3
flash-attention: c68c592fd9da1e40a4fb0b56229caae6754ac5c9
nvidia-cutlass-dsl: 4.7

## Root cause
PR #2559 intentionally introduced new varlen scheduler dispatch behavior.
FlashAttentionForwardSm100 can now select:

1. `DynamicPersistentVarlenScheduler` when dynamic-persistent scheduler metadata is used;
2. `StaticPersistentTileScheduler` when the varlen workload is eligible for static persistence;
3. `SingleTileVarlenScheduler` otherwise.

However, the varlen helpers in `test_clc_fuzz.py` still unconditionally require SingleTileVarlenScheduler:
[check_varlen_output](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/1cc7ff67cbc5685046c75183e8defecca3e35d5c/tests/cute/test_clc_fuzz.py#L305-L330)
[check_varlen_output_seqused](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/1cc7ff67cbc5685046c75183e8defecca3e35d5c/tests/cute/test_clc_fuzz.py#L348-L377)
